title: Signal sweep and interop notes — weekly sync (2026-06-11)
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Sofia, Devon, Cara. Quick sync to capture the week's run-through for tracing / dashboards / cost telemetry experiments.

Purpose: capture decisions from the sampling and dashboard migration experiments, flag regressions, and assign follow-ups before Friday. This doc is a working log (notes + short TODOs).

1) Sampling experiment status (prefix/KV traces)
- Goal: reduce ingest cost without losing signal for high-cardinality regressions.
- What we tried: lowered global trace sampling from 5% -> 1% for background worker spans; kept 100% for all error spans and all requests above 2s latency.
- Observed impact (48h window): estimated trace storage cost reduced by ~28% (billing estimate on s3 + compression), alert noise from low-value worker spans down ~40%.
- Downsides: a couple of mid-priority alerts missed for ephemeral RPC failures — two incidents tied to a flaky batch job (OB-4237). We recovered from logs but lost full KV cache context for one incident.
- Decision: keep 1% for background workers for one more week, add a fallback rule to force-sample spans tied to job IDs in the next rollout if error rate > 0.5% in last 15m.
- Action items:
  * Marco: add forced-sample rule and unit test (JIRA OB-4301) — due 2026-06-15.
  * Sofia: update sampling playbook with step-by-step rollback and example queries — due 2026-06-16.

2) Dashboard migration progress (Grafana -> Console-lite dashboards)
- Migration scope: customer-facing latency dashboards (per-model), cost-per-token trend, and end-to-end request tracing overview.
- Completed: latency & p50/p95 panels migrated; templating variables preserved.
- Work in progress: cost-per-token panel — we need to pull token attribution from billing pipeline (small schema change).
- Risk noted: one panel used a pre-aggregated metric that our new pipeline no longer ships; quick temporary patch implemented in telemetry service to recreate the aggregate (see PR 872).
- Decision: ship latency panels to console-beta while cost panel remains behind a feature flag.
- Action items:
  * Devon: coordinate with billing team for schema change (meet billing team Wed 2026-06-14, invite in calendar).
  * Cara: run visual QA on console-beta for p95 anomalies (write checklist) — due 2026-06-13.

3) Cost telemetry anomalies and root-cause notes
- Observed: tokenization pipeline spike on 2026-06-09 increased token normalization CPU by ~2.8x for a 3-hour window. Estimated incremental cost: ~$4.3k.
- Short-term mitigation: enabled an additional autoscale limiter on the tokenizer cluster; drop in CPU usage evident within 30m of change.
- Root cause hypothesis: a small subset of requests (internal integration tests) started sending extremely long sequences due to a test harness bug.
- Follow-up: add a pre-acceptance check to reject requests > 100k tokens from non-prod clients — Aisha to file an internal policy PR.

4) Tracing fidelity vs latency tradeoff (kernel/driver upgrade surprise)
- Incident: after a minor kernel/driver update on one dedicated pool node, tail inference latency for some large-context models increased ~10–12ms median on that node. Traces showed larger-than-usual queue times in the RPC layer.
- Hypothesis: new NIC driver changed batching behavior for small packets (affects KV cache RPCs).
- Temporary workaround: route traffic for that pool through fallback region until we patch driver config.
- Action items:
  * Marco + platform-engineering: schedule controlled driver test in staging (track under OB-4310).
  * Sofia: add a panel showing per-node queue-time distribution to help detect this class of regressions earlier.

5) Small wins / micro improvements
- Reduced retention on low-value debug traces from 30 days -> 7 days for non-prod namespaces (saves ~9% trace storage).
- Batch sampling flag now togglable per-customer via console feature flag — deployed to canary customers (internal code feature flag id: ff/sampling-per-customer).
- Added a quick query template for SREs to correlate local batching with p95 tail latency (saves ~8–10m for postmortems).

6) Open questions / unresolved
- How aggressive can we get with sampling for non-prod without losing the ability to root-cause across services that share keys? (Sofia to prototype cross-service synthetic traces next week.)
- Do we want automated rollbacks when cost delta > 30% in 1h window for any telemetry pipeline change? (ops/finance sync asked for proposal.)
- Should we maintain a small always-on trace store (1% of total capacity) with full KV context specifically for burst/regression hunts?

7) Upcoming items & calendar
- 2026-06-14: billing schema sync (Devon + billing).
- 2026-06-15: sampling force-sample rule merged (Marco).
- 2026-06-16: playbook update + QA checklist complete (Sofia/Cara).
- Next sync: 2026-06-18, 10:00am PT (tentative).

8) Decisions summary (for changelog)
- Keep background worker sampling at 1% for another week with forced-sampling-on-error rule.
- Deploy latency dashboards to console-beta; cost panel behind flag until billing schema is updated.
- Route traffic off the affected driver-upgraded pool until patch validated.

9) Quick checklist for oncall (put in runbook)
- If tokenization CPU > 2x baseline for > 30m: check recent deploys, run the long-seq query, disable non-prod long-seq sources.
- If p95 tail increases > 15ms in a single pool: shift routing to fallback and open OB-4310.
- If trace ingest cost increases > 20% week-over-week: revert sampling change and page observability-sre.

Notes / context links:
- OB-4237: batch-job flaky retries (see incident notes).
- OB-4301: sampling forced rule (in backlog).
- PR 872: temporary aggregate patch (telemetry repo).

If anything needs to be appended mid-week, add comments inline below with initials and date.

-- Aisha K. (notes, live) 2026-06-11
